text:
OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini on April 16, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. The launch signaled a direction for frontier reasoning models characterized by native integration of vision and tool use (such as web search and code interpreter) directly into the model architecture, rather than adding them later [Source: ev-1]. It also established an API-first availability strategy where o3 was initially excluded from the ChatGPT app but available to developers via API [Source: ev-1].

The release demonstrated that OpenAI could defend its position against competitors like DeepSeek and Anthropic by reframing frontier capability as "tool-using reasoning at commodity prices" [Source: ev-1]. This is evidenced by aggressive pricing structures, with o4-mini costing $1.10 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens, compared to o3's $10/$40 rates [Source: ev-1]. Furthermore, the launch highlighted a shift toward efficient compute allocation through "budget forcing," which uses task-adaptive dynamic compute so that harder questions require more thinking time [Source: ev-1]. The models also introduced OpenAI’s first private chain-of-thought policy, keeping reasoning tokens hidden from API callers [Source: ev-1].

In terms of performance, o3 set a record on the ARC-AGI benchmark by achieving approximately 87.5% on ARC-AGI-1 at high compute levels, surpassing or meeting the ~85% human baseline and becoming the first model to reach this threshold [Source: ev-1].
